newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tunisian rights activist free after day in custody.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian rights activist free after day in custody.

text.p: Salah Zeghidi, vice-president of the Tunisian League for the Defence of Human Rights, has been freed by police after a day in custody in Tunis but may later be re-arrested, human rights activists said on Wednesday.
Zeghidi was freed by the Tunisian authorities late on Tuesday evening but police told him before letting him go that he would later be charged with unspecified law violations, the activists said.

The police also kept his passport, according to officials of the Paris-based International Federation of Human Rights (FIDH) and the Paris-based Committee for the Respect of Freedom and the Rights of Man in Tunisia (CRLDHT).
Zeghidi had been detained at Tunis airport on Monday evening as he returned home after criticising his government at a Paris meeting.
The FIDH said Zeghidi had voiced concern about human rights in Tunisia at the Paris meeting of major civil rights groups.
Voicing concern that he could be mistreated, FIDH had said the Tunisian government would be held responsible if Zeghidi were tortured or hurt.
Tunisia has in the past reacted angrily to criticism of its human rights record.
Five international human rights watchdog groups, including Amnesty International, accused Tunisia last month of widespread and worsening rights violations against political opponents.
They said some prominent human rights activists had been prevented from leaving the country while others had been arrested, questioned and threatened with prosecution.
In May, the European Parliament also expressed concern over the harassment of political opponents and their families and the absence of press freedom in the North African country.
